Analytical Profiles

Elham Ebrahimi

Source: vignettes/articles/profiles.Rmd
profiles.Rmd

Reproducible workflows for monitoring networks

Standardised sampling protocols and interoperable data do not guarantee comparable ecological estimates. Differences in analytical methods, parameter settings, and processing rules can affect results and their interpretation.

Analytical Profiles provide reusable workflows tailored to the objectives and sampling protocols of individual monitoring networks or projects. Each profile brings together agreed analytical methods, assumptions, settings, and reporting conventions, supporting consistency across researchers, sites, and monitoring rounds.

Profiles can reuse existing analytical modules or incorporate new ones, with methodological changes explicitly documented.

Available profiles

camtrapReport currently provides two profiles: default, for general ecological reporting, and EOW, for European Observatory of Wildlife–oriented reporting. Additional network-specific profiles based on community-agreed analytical workflows are under development.

Generate a report

First create a camReport object using camData() (see Get started).

library(camtrapReport)

# General ecological report (default profile)
report(cm, view = TRUE)

# EOW-oriented ecological report
report(cm, profile = "EOW", view = TRUE, format = "PDF")

Explore available modules 

# List available profiles
profile_names(cm)

# Inspect the modules used by a profile
section_names(object = cm, profile = "EOW")

Explore the Module Catalog for descriptions of available analytical and reporting modules.

Contribute an Analytical Profile

We invite camera-trap monitoring networks and research projects worldwide to contribute their established analytical workflows.

Contributors should document their agreed analytical methods, assumptions, parameter settings, and reporting conventions. The camtrapReport development team can collaborate with them to implement and test these workflows as reusable Analytical Profiles, with methodological changes documented to support long-term reproducibility.

Propose a profile or discuss a collaboration.
